professors.name: Jürgen Schmidhuber
professors.title: Professor of Computer Science; Co-Chair, Center of Excellence for Generative AI
professors.biography: Official KAUST profile states that Professor Schmidhuber is co-chair of the Center of Excellence for Generative AI and a professor in the Computer Science Program. The profile also states that he served as Scientific Director of the Swiss AI Lab IDSIA and, at KAUST, leads AI research projects, contributes to AI-related educational programs, and engages with public and private sector organizations.
professors.research_summary: Official profile describes research on AI applications across health care, drug design, chemistry, materials science, natural language processing, automation, robotics and soft robotics, and a long-term ambition to build self-improving AI.

professors.name: Xin Gao
professors.title: Professor of Computer Science; Co-Chair, Center of Excellence for Smart Health
professors.biography: Official KAUST profile lists Professor Gao as Professor of Computer Science and Co-Chair of the Center of Excellence for Smart Health, with membership in the Bioinformatics Platform.
professors.research_summary: Official profile states research at the intersection of computer science and biology, including machine learning theories related to large language models, deep learning, probabilistic graphical models, kernel methods and matrix factorization, and AI solutions for biomedicine, biomedical imaging and omics-based disease detection.

professors.name: Peter Richtárik
professors.title: Professor of Computer Science
professors.biography: Official KAUST profile identifies Professor Richtárik as a professor in the Computer Science Program whose work on randomized and distributed optimization algorithms contributed to the foundations of machine learning and federated learning.
professors.research_summary: Official profile lists research at the intersection of mathematics, computer science, machine learning, optimization, numerical linear algebra and high-performance computing, including randomized coordinate descent, stochastic gradient methods and federated learning over private data.

professors.name: Mohamed Elhoseiny
professors.title: Associate Professor of Computer Science
professors.biography: Official KAUST profile states that Associate Professor Elhoseiny is principal investigator of the KAUST Vision-CAIR Research Group. He joined CEMSE at KAUST in 2019 after a visiting faculty role at Baidu Research and a postdoctoral position at Facebook AI Research (2016–2019).
professors.research_summary: Official profile describes primary research in computer vision, the intersection of natural language and vision, computational creativity, efficient multimodal learning with limited data, and vision and language, including MiniGPT-related work listed on the official page.

professors.name: Francesco Orabona
professors.title: Associate Professor of Computer Science
professors.biography: Official KAUST profile states that Professor Orabona joined KAUST from Boston University's Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering and is a leading researcher in parameter-free online optimization. He has served as an area chair for NeurIPS, ICML, COLT and ICLR.
professors.research_summary: Official profile describes research combining practical and theoretical machine learning, including online learning, optimization, statistical learning theory, and parameter-free machine learning algorithms that function without expensive hand-tuned parameters.

professors.name: Peter Wonka
professors.title: Professor of Computer Science
professors.biography: Official KAUST profile states that Professor Wonka joined KAUST in 2011 and is a Full Professor of Computer Science. He has held roles as CS Program Chair and Interim Director of the Visual Computing Center, and is listed as affiliated with the Center of Excellence for Generative AI.
professors.research_summary: Official profile lists research in computer vision, computer graphics, remote sensing and machine learning, with current focus on deep learning, generative modeling of images, videos and 3D scenes, 3D reconstruction, 3D computer vision, and 3D vision and language.

professors.name: Robert Hoehndorf
professors.title: Associate Professor of Computer Science
professors.biography: Official KAUST profile identifies Associate Professor Hoehndorf as principal investigator of the Bio-Ontology Research Group (BORG). He joined KAUST in 2014 after research positions at Aberystwyth University, the University of Cambridge and the European Bioinformatics Institute.
professors.research_summary: Official profile describes research in knowledge representation, neuro-symbolic methods and their application in life sciences, including DeepGO methods for protein function prediction and neuro-symbolic methods for ontologies and knowledge graphs.

professors.name: Bernard Ghanem
professors.title: Professor of Electrical and Computer Engineering; Chair, Center of Excellence for Generative AI
professors.biography: Official KAUST profile states that Professor Ghanem is Chair of the KAUST Center of Excellence for Generative AI, a professor of Electrical and Computer Engineering, and principal investigator of the Image and Video Understanding Lab. Official program affiliations include ECE and Computer Science.
professors.research_summary: Official profile describes research in computer vision and machine learning, including large-scale video understanding, 3D scene comprehension, neural network robustness and certification (trustworthy AI), continual learning, and foundational models in vision and language.

professors.name: Dominik L. Michels
professors.title: Associate Professor of Computer Science
professors.biography: Official KAUST profile states that Professor Michels founded the Computational Sciences Group at KAUST after postdoctoral work at Caltech and a period in the Computer Science Department at Stanford University. He joined KAUST in 2016.
professors.research_summary: Official profile describes research on efficient algorithms for accurate simulation of natural phenomena and technical procedures, including algorithmics, artificial intelligence, machine learning, computer graphics, physics-based modeling and numerical analysis.

professors.name: Wolfgang Heidrich
professors.title: Professor of Computer Science and Electrical and Computer Engineering
professors.biography: Official KAUST profile states that Professor Heidrich is a professor of Computer Science and Electrical and Computer Engineering, a member of the KAUST Visual Computing Center, and served as its director from 2014 to 2021. He is listed as affiliated with the Center of Excellence for Generative AI.
professors.research_summary: Official profile describes research in computational imaging and display, combining computer graphics, machine vision, imaging, inverse methods, optics and perception, including end-to-end learned imaging systems.

professors.name: Di Wang
professors.title: Assistant Professor of Computer Science
professors.biography: Official KAUST profile lists Di Wang as Assistant Professor of Computer Science and adjunct professor of Statistics, affiliated with the Center of Excellence for Generative AI. Official page names Privacy Awareness, Responsibility and Trustworthy Lab; a dedicated official lab URL was not used as affiliation in this pass, so lab is null.
professors.research_summary: Official biography: privacy-preserving machine learning, interpretability, machine learning theory, and trustworthy machine learning, including differentially private, adversarial, and interpretable machine learning. Official current interests: trustworthy machine learning and large models, including controllable and editable memorization.

professors.name: Marco Canini
professors.title: Professor of Computer Science
professors.biography: Official KAUST profile lists Marco Canini as Professor of Computer Science. Official research interests name Software-Defined Advanced Networked and Distributed Systems (SANDS). The fetched official faculty page did not publish an email address.
professors.research_summary: Official research interests: principled construction and operation of large-scale networked computer systems (SANDS), including distributed systems, large-scale/cloud computing, and programmable networks. Official keyword tags: machine learning, artificial intelligence, distributed systems, large-scale computing, cloud computing.

professors.name: Ali Shoker
professors.title: Research Associate Professor of Computer Science
professors.biography: Official KAUST profile lists Ali Shoker as Research Associate Professor leading the Cyber Security and Resilience Technology (CyberSaR) Lab. Official keyword tags include trustworthy AI. A dedicated CyberSaR website URL was not independently confirmed, so lab is null.
professors.research_summary: Official biography describes cybersecurity and resilience by design using distributed systems, hardware, and trustworthy AI. Official keywords include cybersecurity, cyber-resilience, and trustworthy AI.
